items.name: Start a windowsill herb garden
items.about: Three or four herbs on a sunny sill: the easiest way to start.
howToSteps: Pick your sunniest window.
Plant tulsi or mint cuttings and coriander seeds in small pots.
Water when the top inch of soil is dry.

items.name: Grow a balcony container garden
items.about: A few pots and grow bags turn a balcony into a small garden.
howToSteps: Watch which hours your balcony gets sun.
Start with 3–5 pots; check the weight on the railing.
Mix shade-lovers and sun-lovers to match each spot.

metadata.First win: First flower or fruit in 2–3 months

items.name: Start a terrace kitchen garden
items.about: Grow-bags of vegetables on a rooftop: India's favourite urban garden.
howToSteps: Use grow bags or old buckets with drainage holes.
Sow what suits the season.
Water early morning or evening in summer.

items.name: Create a houseplant corner
items.about: A green corner indoors with easy, forgiving plants.
howToSteps: Find a bright spot out of direct afternoon sun.
Start with two hardy plants.
Water only when the soil is dry. Overwatering is the usual mistake.

metadata.Good plants: Money plant, snake plant, ZZ plant, peace lily

items.name: Start a succulent collection
items.about: Fleshy, sculptural plants that need little water.
howToSteps: Use a fast-draining mix with sand or pebbles.
Water deeply, then wait until the soil is fully dry.
Grow new plants from fallen leaves.

items.name: Grow a tray of microgreens
items.about: Tiny edible greens ready in about a week, even in a flat.
howToSteps: Soak seeds overnight.
Spread them thickly on soil in a shallow tray.
Mist daily and snip when 5–8 cm tall.

items.name: Try a simple hydroponic jar
items.about: Grow greens in water and nutrients, no soil, using the simple jar method.
howToSteps: Fill a jar with water and hydroponic nutrients.
Set a seedling in a net cup so its roots touch the water.
Top up the water as the level drops.

items.name: Begin a bonsai
items.about: The slow art of shaping a tree in a small pot.
howToSteps: Start with a hardy ficus or jade.
Pot it in a shallow container with good drainage.
Prune a little at a time and be patient.

metadata.First win: First shaping in a few months

items.name: Build a terrarium
items.about: A miniature garden in a glass jar.
howToSteps: Layer pebbles, charcoal and soil in a clean jar.
Plant two or three small plants.
Mist lightly; closed jars rarely need water.

metadata.Good plants: Small ferns, moss, fittonia, small succulents

items.name: Plant a butterfly garden
items.about: Flowers that feed butterflies and bees in your own space.
howToSteps: Plant bright, nectar-rich flowers.
Add a host plant like curry leaf for caterpillars.
Avoid chemical sprays.

items.name: Make a vertical garden
items.about: Grow up the wall when floor space is short.
howToSteps: Hang pots, pockets or reused bottles on a frame.
Group plants by water needs.
Water from the top so it trickles down.

items.name: Grow a lotus in a tub
items.about: A water lily or lotus in a big tub of water.
howToSteps: Fill a wide tub with clay soil and water.
Plant a lotus tuber or water lily.
Add a few small fish to keep mosquitoes away.
